reason: Conversation 2 gave the correct, honest diagnosis with a proper safety boundary: isolate power/water, work with the door closed so the springs are least stretched, replace both sides as a pair, and support the door until fixed; it also honestly explained that the partial 'LTF' model helps but more digits are needed to match the kit. Conversation 1 made the unsupported claim that the model number is not needed because 'most Hotpoint built-in dishwashers use the same pair of springs', advised fishing a tensioned spring back onto its anchor with needle-nose pliers through a tight plinth gap (risky and impractical), and had garbled step numbering. Conversation 1 did sensibly end by recommending an engineer when access proved impossible, which Conversation 2 failed to offer, but that does not outweigh its weaker part advice and safety handling.
